question: Who wrote ‘Gita Rahasya’, which is a commentary on the Bhagavad-Gita, in the Mandalay jail of Myanmar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, **also known as Lokmanya Tilak or** "The Maker of Modern India" **by Mahatma Gandhi, wrote the book Gita Rahasya.
 
• Geeta Rahasya is the analysis of karma-yoga in the Bhagat Gita, which is known to be the gift of the Vedas and the Upanishad.
 
• It includes: 
 
 
• an external examination of the Gita 
 
• the original Sanskrit stanzas
 
• their Marathi translation 
 
• commentaries on the stanzas, and
 
• a comparison of Eastern with Western doctrines etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak **was a leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was also called the Father of Indian Unrest.
 
• Tilak joined Congress in 1890.
 
• He was opposed to moderate ways and views and had a more radical and aggressive stance against British rule.
 
 
• The extremists led by him.
 
 
 
• He gave the slogan, “Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.”
 
• He believed that no progress was possible without self-rule.
 
• He was part of the extremist faction of the INC and was a proponent of boycotts and Swadeshi movements.
 
• He published two papers – Kesari in Marathi and Mahratta in English.
